A:gaunt-peter:father.note: Husband of Lydia Gaunt and probable father of Hananiah. Their family is described by Sandwich Friends historical research and the published Barnstable probate abstract of Lydia's will. Exact birth/death dates and Lincoln ancestry remain unresolved; do not substitute the speculative Hampton maiden surname for Lydia.

A:gaunt-lydia:mother.note: Her will dated 28 Dec 1691 and proved 21 Apr 1692 explicitly names sons Israel, Zachariah and Hannaniah, plus daughter Lydia and grandchildren. Source: Barnstable probate records 1:66–67, abstracted by Gustavus Adolphus Hinckley, as transcribed on WeRelate. Published abstract accessed live; original probate image not accessed. Maiden surname unknown.21 Apr 1692 is the probate date, not an established death date.

A:benjamin-hulsey:father.note: The original 1880 census records B. F. Hulsey, a thirty-two-year-old miner born in Georgia, with wife Sarah G., 30, born Arkansas, and son George W., 4, in Center Township, Montgomery County, Arkansas. George’s December 1875 birth in the 1900 Sulphur Springs census and 24 December 1875 birth on his 1918 draft card are consistent with the child’s age. An unsourced 1977 family query links a Benjamin F. to George Washington, but contains conflicting names and dates and does not prove the connection. The connection remains probable: no record yet explicitly connects the adult George, husband of Sarah Rebecca Graves, to the named 1880 parents. This household has not been securely identified with the separate Benjamin Franklin Hulsey biography or with Sylvania Partain.

A:balas-newton:father.note: The original 1889 Etowah County marriage papers identify Balas Newton as Lizzie Newton’s father. The 1880 Etowah census lists Balus Newton and daughter Elizabeth, aged seven; its rare name, place and age make this a probable match, although the census and marriage papers do not contain a second unique identifier. The census lists his wife Mary; her identification as Lizzie’s mother is probable.

A:sarah-g-hulsey:mother.note: The original 1880 census lists Sarah G., 30, born Arkansas, as the wife of B. F. Hulsey, in the household containing his son George W., 4. She is a probable mother or stepmother of that child; the census names her as wife, not explicitly as his biological mother. The identification of this child with the later George Washington Hulsey remains probable. Hulsey is her married surname; her maiden name and full given names are unknown. She is not Sarah Rebecca Graves, George’s later wife, and has not been identified with Sylvania Susane Partain.

A:bridget-croasdale:mother.note: Potts (1895), p. 29, lists Bridget among Thomas and Agnes Croasdale’s children, using birth dates supplied from Settle Monthly Meeting; the book notes that Middletown dates vary. The Middletown register transcription names John and Bridget as Elizabeth Cowgill’s parents. The original meeting-register image has not yet been independently reread. The connection is marked probable.

A:thomas-croasdale:father.note: Potts (1895), pp. 25–29, reproduces the Settle certificate, estate inventory and children’s list. The inventory supports a 1684 death; the 1682 date in some later accounts conflicts with it. His own birth date and parentage have not been established from an independently examined original register.

A:agnes-hawthornthwaite:mother.note: Potts (1895) gives Agnes’s marriage to Thomas, names her in the Settle certificate and reproduces her estate inventory. Her surname appears in variant forms, including Hathernthwaite. The printed inventory date conflicts with the reported death and administration chronology; that inconsistency remains unresolved. Her parents are not attached.

A:thomas-mercer:father.note: The original Ringwood Quaker birth entry, TNA RG6/1027 image 18/206, handwritten p. 6, has been visually reviewed and names Thomas and Ann Mercer of Ringwood as parents of Ann, born on the 24th day of the 12th month 1666 (24 Feb 1666/7). Identifying this child with the later Pennsylvania wife of William Brown, and this father with Thomas of Andover/Aston, remains probable. His own parents are unknown. The 1709 Yearly Meeting catalogue, independently read in its 1979 printed transcription (PGM31:120), directly names the immigrant Anne Browne as Thomas Mercer’s daughter and says she came with him. It remembers her among deceased Public Friends; the original manuscript has not been examined. The Ringwood-to-immigrant identification remains probable.

A:ann-mercer:mother.note: The original Ringwood birth register names Ann and Thomas Mercer of Ringwood as the parents of the child Ann, born on the 24th day of the 12th month 1666 (24 Feb 1666/7). No maiden surname is given. Identification with the mother of William Brown’s later Pennsylvania wife remains probable. Her maiden surname and life dates remain unknown; Mercer is not asserted as her maiden surname.

A:richard-browne:father.note: The original Wellingborough birth register, TNA RG6/1380 image 20/150, names Richard Browne as Willyam’s father, with birth on the 29th day of the first month 1658. It names no mother. This register entry has been visually reviewed; the Northamptonshire Quarterly Meeting entry and the varying maternal names in later accounts remain to be checked. Identifying the English child with the Pennsylvania emigrant remains probable. No earlier parents or exact life dates are assigned to Richard.

A:margaret-m-hulsey:1880.note: Recorded as a child of B. F. Hulsey in the 1880 Center Township household, Montgomery County, Arkansas. Margaret was six and Charles five months old. They are probable siblings of the later George Washington Hulsey because identification of the four-year-old George in this household with the adult George remains probable. Sarah G. is recorded as the wife of the household head, not explicitly as the children’s biological mother; no mother is attached here. This child has not been merged with a similarly named person in the 1900 census.

A:charles-f-hulsey:1880.note: Recorded as a child of B. F. Hulsey in the 1880 Center Township household, Montgomery County, Arkansas. Margaret was six and Charles five months old. They are probable siblings of the later George Washington Hulsey because identification of the four-year-old George in this household with the adult George remains probable. Sarah G. is recorded as the wife of the household head, not explicitly as the children’s biological mother; no mother is attached here. A:joel-john-thompson:brother.note: Dawes Card 1283 records this child in Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson’s household and refers the parents to the first two entries. Joel’s 1937 Indian-Pioneer interview names those parents and supplies his birth date. His death date appears on the shared Joel John and Ira Mae Thompson headstone. The young studio portrait is attributed by an Ancestry tree tag, not an inscription on this crop.

A:peter-pitchlynn-thompson:brother.note: Dawes Card 1283 records this child in Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson’s household and refers the parents to the first two entries. Joel’s 1937 interview names his brother Peter Pitchlyn. The approximate birth and 1979 death year come from the High Hill cemetery transcription; that stone remains to be checked independently.

A:ella-n-thompson:sister.note: Dawes Card 1283 records this child in Joseph P. and Betsy Thompson’s household and refers the parents to the first two entries. Joseph’s 13 April 1901 sworn affidavit identifies Ella as his daughter and gives her death as 22 May 1899. Her birth is estimated from the age on the card.

A:edith-irene-thompson:sister.note: Her family memorial in the May 2012 Biskinik, p. 16, names her parents as Simon and Francis Thompson and her deceased brother Junior. Francis is the spelling printed in the memorial; the mother is recorded elsewhere as Frances Pisachubbe.

A:james-calvin-stevenson.note: Elam Stevenson’s will and the Goodspeed family sketch name both James C. and Abner A. as sons of Elam. The 1912 Andrews autobiography names James C. and Margaret C. as Eliza Catherine Stevenson’s parents.

A:margaret-caroline-brown.note: The 1912 autobiography by her son-in-law W. T. Andrews names Margaret C. Stevenson as Eliza Catherine’s mother. Her maiden name and dates are from published family histories; her parents are not attached.

A:eliza-catherine-stevenson.note: Her husband W. T. Andrews named her parents and their son James David in his 1912 autobiography. James David’s 1937 obituary independently names William Thomas and Eliza Stevenson Andrews as his parents.

A:william-thomas-andrews.note: In his 1912 autobiography he identifies his wife Eliza Catherine Stevenson, her parents James C. and Margaret C., and their son James David.

A:james-david-andrews.note: His father’s 1912 autobiography names him, and his 1937 Pulaski Citizen obituary names his parents and son Major General Frank M. Andrews. Nashville Public Library’s family papers identify Frank Maxwell Andrews as a son of James David and Lula Maxwell.

A:lula-adaline-maxwell.note: Nashville Public Library’s finding aid identifies Lula Adaline Maxwell Andrews and James D. Andrews as Frank Maxwell Andrews’s parents.

A:frank-maxwell-andrews.note: James David’s obituary names his son Major General Frank M. Andrews; Nashville Public Library’s family papers identify him as Frank Maxwell Andrews. W. T. Andrews’s own 1912 memoir names James David’s mother and grandparents, connecting this branch to Elam and Lydia Stevenson.

A:mary-dockery:newton.note: Mary Ann Dockery married Bailus Newton in 1867. The 1880 census records Balus Newton, wife Mary and a daughter Elizabeth, seven. Their identification with Lizzie Newton and her father Balas, named in the 1889 marriage papers, is probable; the census does not explicitly say Mary was Elizabeth’s mother. An Alabama death index names Mary Marzee Dockery as the mother of Oda Verbena Newton, a possible match for the youngest child in the household.
